newsitem.title: CHINA: China preparing new list of B share companies.
newsitem.headline: China preparing new list of B share companies.

text.p: China could approve soon another batch of companies seeking B share listings on domestic stock exchanges, Ma Zhongzhi, director of the executive office of the State Council's Securities Committee, said on Wednesday.
"It is very hard to give a timetable but I would expect by the year-end," he said in answer to questions about further B share offers.
Ma, who was speaking to reporters during a business conference, did not give any indication of how many companies might get approval for listing or say when the actual listing might be made.
Securities sources say some 80 companies have applied to offer foreign currency denominated B shares for foreign investors on the nation's markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen near Hong Kong.

Ma said that the B share companies should be large in size and relatively well managed -- similar requirements that market regulators have given for so-called H share companies to be listed in Hong Kong.
Market sources said, however, that larger and better managed companies would prefer to list in Hong Kong, and China might have trouble finding such qualified companies for domestic listings.
Ma also said that policy makers were also concerned about the possible market response to the offers, particularly on the extremely weak Shanghai market for B shares.
"We are watching this situation," he said.

The Shanghai B share index has hit successive record lows of late though it rebounded slightly over the last two days. It ended at 46.20, up 0.686 point, on Wednesday on turnover of only $2.6 million.

Securities industries sources said that many of the companies looking for a domestic listing are hoping to have their shares traded on the Shenzhen bourse, which has held up better than Shanghai's B share market.
